name: Hand Fighting
description: Win the hand fight to control wrists, inside ties, underhooks, and head position. Hand fighting is the battle for control that happens before any technique — whoever wins the hand fight dictates the engagement.
shortInstruction: Win the inside tie, secure wrist control, fight for the underhook, and establish head position. If you lose a grip, pummel back inside immediately — do not fight from outside position.
summary: Hand fighting is the invisible battle of grip, wrist, and arm control that determines who initiates the takedown, guard pass, or guard pull. The key principles are: (1) inside control beats outside control — your hand between their arm and body controls their center, (2) two-on-one beats one-on-one — use both hands on one of their arms to create advantages, (3) pummel back immediately when you lose inside position — do not grab from outside, (4) head position controls body position — the underhook requires head control to be effective.
whyItWorks: Inside position (your hand between their arm and body) gives you mechanical advantage — you control their center line
Two-on-one (both hands on one of their arms) creates a local strength advantage that neutralizes their other arm
The underhook is the most valuable hand fight win because it gives you control of their upper body
Head position (forehead to their jaw) prevents them from posting on your head and breaks their posture
commonMistakes: Grabbing from outside position (reaching around their arms) — this is weaker than pummeling to inside
Fighting hand-to-hand (one-on-one) against a stronger opponent — use two-on-one to negate strength
Losing the hand fight and then trying to force a takedown from a compromised position
Ignoring head position — hand control without head control is incomplete
safetySummary: Hand fighting can lead to finger injuries if you grip aggressively — keep fingers safe by gripping with the palm, not the fingertips
Do not lock your fingers or grip so tight that you cannot release quickly — locked grips in standing can cause shoulder injuries when the opponent moves suddenly
Avoid eye pokes — keep your hands visible and controlled during hand fighting exchanges

systemLogic.corePrinciple: Hand fighting determines who initiates the engagement. The priority hierarchy is: Inside Tie → Wrist Control → Underhook → Head Position. If you lose any priority, pummel back inside — never fight from outside position.

decisionTree.condition: Opponent has inside tie (their hand between your arm and body)
decisionTree.action: Pummel your arm back inside by circling your elbow under theirs. Do not reach around or grab from outside — the inside hand always wins the grip fight.

decisionTree.condition: Opponent controls both of your wrists
decisionTree.action: Free one hand with a wrist spin rotation, then establish two-on-one control on their lead arm. Two-on-one creates a local strength advantage that neutralizes their other arm.
Set your stance wider and keep your hands up. Head position controls body position — if they control your head, they control your posture.

decisionTree.condition: Opponent is stronger in the collar tie
decisionTree.action: Switch to an overhook or two-on-one to neutralize their strength advantage. Do not fight strength with strength — change the grip.
Switch to a far-side underhook (reach under their far arm) or use a whizzer (overhook) to counter their underhook. Drive your shoulder into their chest to re-flatten them.

exitStrategies: If you keep losing the hand fight, drill pummeling entries — you are reaching instead of pummeling.
If the opponent is stronger in the hand fight, use two-on-one on their lead arm to neutralize their strength advantage.
Hand control without head position is incomplete — always pair hand fighting with forehead-to-jaw head position.

moneyDetails: Hand fighting determines the outcome of most grappling matches before any technique is attempted
Winning the hand fight against a stronger opponent requires technique (pummeling, two-on-one) not strength
Hand fighting is the most under-trained skill in BJJ — mastering it gives you an immediate advantage over most opponents
fixItFast: If they keep grabbing your wrists: use a wrist spin to free your hand and re-establish inside position
If they are stronger in the collar tie: switch to an overhook or two-on-one
If they keep snapping your head: set your stance wider and keep your hands up
